A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NVGS, with matching methods and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary sections support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering comparisons, ablations, timing measurements and per-asset evaluations in the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds TEMPLES results and rasterizer diagnostics in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The visibility-extraction procedure, two-MLP representation, FoV correction and instanced culling pipeline remain unchanged. v2 specifies previously undocumented network, input and loss details without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds the temple asset and downscaled TEMPLES layout, extending evaluation to a detailed architectural asset with approximately 1.3 million Gaussians before pruning. FOREST, CROWD and DONUTSEA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain gsplat, radius-clipped gsplat, V3DG and the instanced rasterizer without the MLP. TEMPLES uses this existing set. Newly cited MaskGaussian and Splatshop are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added evaluation compares TEMPLES FLIP against both gsplat and the rasterizer without the MLP, and introduces rasterizer-only pixel-difference checks (Figures 12–13). These controls separate visibility-prediction errors from rasterizer discrepancies. Existing benchmark metrics, downscaling and hardware are retained; newly disclosed training details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an asset-complexity evaluation and diagnoses large-floater discrepancies using MLP-disabled rendering and difference images. The existing sampling, offset, auxiliary-view, FoV and radius-clipping ablations, together with the SH-degree analysis, are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging across views, distances and assets remains the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes five SSIM entries from 1.000 to 0.999. Added TEMPLES results report NVGS PSNR 40.95, FLIP 0.029 and VRAM 3.1 GB, versus V3DG's 52.30, 0.004 and 10.3 GB (v2 Table 4), alongside new distance curves and difference images. Existing ablation and per-asset values are unchanged. Table 2's timing conversions and Table 1's VRAM precision changes are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The visibility-contribution definition and Equations 1–2 for camera distance and FoV/scale correction are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same rendering, memory, image-quality and scalability claims. The conclusion replaces 'the first object-level occlusion culling' with 'a novel object-level occlusion culling approach,' dropping the explicit priority claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds explanations involving Gaussian density and tile coverage, while A.4 attributes TEMPLES reference-image discrepancies primarily to rasterizer handling of large floaters. Section 4.3 also proposes combining near-distance V3DG bundles with NVGS. Existing visibility-complexity and distance limitations are retained and expanded.

D1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.1 fill important reproducibility gaps: embedding inputs, 2000 sampled views, 5-degree cones, architecture and ReLU activations for both MLPs, frequency-weighted BCE, and fragment/transmittance thresholds. v1 described only the embedding network's size and omitted the loss. However, v2 removes v1's explicit 30,000-iteration training budget.

R1.justification: v2 adds MaskGaussian to the pruning discussion and Splatshop to a broader discussion of renderer optimizations. The central positioning against global pruning and LoD remains. Other reference changes predominantly update bibliographic information and style.

P1.justification: Extensive sentence and paragraph rewrites span the introduction, related work, method, experiments and supplement. Related-work discussion is reordered, the method overview is condensed into numbered components, and bibliography formatting is standardized. The main section sequence remains, while the supplement becomes Appendix A with additional subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds TEMPLES Table 4 and Figures 12–13. The previous per-asset table and large-scene figures are retained with renumbering and relocation. Several qualitative plates are reformatted, and Table 2 adopts minute–second notation; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through important network, loss and sampling disclosures, and adds a useful complex-asset evaluation with controls exposing rasterizer/reference discrepancies. These gains are tempered by removal of the 30,000-iteration budget and retention of broad image-quality superiority claims despite V3DG's better TEMPLES reference metrics. The revision provides a limited net improvement without changing the core method or most existing evidence.
